title: Biases in Large Language Model-Elicited Text: A Case Study in Natural Language Inference

bias_targets.methodology: Training hypothesis-only classifiers (Naive Bayes and fine-tuned BERT) to detect spurious correlations and using conditional probability to identify 'give-away' words that act as artifacts indicative of specific NLI labels.

Calculating Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) to identify words in the generated hypotheses that are most strongly associated with gender-related query terms (e.g., 'man', 'woman') to expose stereotypical associations.
Calculating Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) to identify word associations with race and ethnicity-related query terms (e.g., 'african', 'asian') in the generated text.
Using Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) to measure semantic associations between age-related query terms (e.g., 'elderly', 'young', 'teenagers') and other words in the generated textual hypotheses.
